data.narrative:
Natilus is a Series A-stage autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $16M to date. The broader sector comprises eight private companies at various stages, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro, with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

Given the limited availability of same-stage, same-tier peers in this sector, peer-median valuation proved inapplicable; a statistically reliable comparable set could not be assembled. Instead, stage-progression methodology was employed as the primary valuation anchor. This approach applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $16M total raised as a proxy for pre-Series A value, yielding an implied post-money valuation of $32M. This multiplier reflects typical venture-scale advancement from seed/pre-seed through Series A.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $27M (low) to $37M (high), with a central estimate of $32M post-money. The primary uncertainty stems from the scarcity of directly comparable transaction data in autonomous systems at this stage and scale. Valuation confidence would materially improve with additional data on recent Series A closings within narrow peer cohorts or public-market multiples applicable to early-stage drone/autonomous technology companies.
